about.title: Ontario Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Ontario sits where the I-10 San Bernardino Freeway, the I-15 Ontario Freeway and the SR-60 Pomona Freeway all pass through one city, and Euclid Avenue carries much of the local traffic in between. Public records for 2025 list 1,083 injury collisions inside city limits, with 1,541 people hurt and 18 lives lost. Reports cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when commuters, freight traffic and shift changes overlap. If one of those crashes was yours, the days that follow can feel like a second collision: calls from an adjuster, a car you cannot drive, medical bills arriving before you know how badly you are hurt. LawProactive exists to take one task off that list. We are not a law firm. We connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who handles San Bernardino County car accident claims and who charges nothing unless your case recovers money. That leaves you free to focus on getting better.

whyChoose.title: Why Ontario Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock matters in California
items.desc: Most California car accident claims must be filed within two years of the crash, but if a city, county or state vehicle was involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. Getting connected early keeps those deadlines from slipping.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover even if you share some blame, with your recovery reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No fee unless your case recovers
items.desc: Every attorney in the LawProactive network works on contingency, and our connection service costs you nothing. There is also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard California car accident case.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement about my crash on the I-10. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shrink your claim. Politely take their contact information and let your attorney handle the conversation.

items.question: What evidence should I hold onto after a car accident in Ontario?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles, the scene and your injuries, plus the police report number from Ontario PD or the CHP. Save every medical record, receipt and message from any insurer, and write down what you remember while it is fresh. If a nearby business or dashcam may have captured the crash, note that too, since footage is often overwritten within days.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we connect you with an independent personal injury attorney in the San Bernardino County area. That attorney works on contingency, meaning you owe no attorney fee unless your case results in a recovery.
